editorial_thesis: The useful frontier is becoming inspectable: composable runtimes, enforceable supply-chain policy, incident-shaped evaluation controls, and formal evidence make agent work easier to try without making trust implicit.

topic_groups.title: Agent Runtime Composition
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh September 10 runtime signal: managed agent loops, persistent sandboxes, regional placement, and current-web search now compose into a practical deployment surface.

sources.title: Build with OpenAI Agents API on Vercel
sources.why_selected: It separates orchestration from execution and supports persistent workspaces with scale-to-zero behavior.
sources.usefulness: Prototype a dossier or client QA agent that returns files and evidence, with promotion owned by a separate review step.

sources.title: Vercel Sandbox is now available in all regions
sources.why_selected: Execution location becomes part of latency, residency, and resilience policy rather than a hidden default.
sources.usefulness: Add region and failover to a client agent architecture review checklist.

sources.title: Tako Search is free on AI Gateway through September 30
sources.why_selected: Current research becomes a tool contract instead of a bespoke retrieval integration.
sources.usefulness: Use it for a bounded comparison of source freshness and citation completeness in daily ingest.

sources.title: OpenAI Agents API sample application
sources.why_selected: Reference code reduces the gap between architecture diagrams and a runnable pilot.
sources.usefulness: Mine the queue/reconnection pattern for scheduled jobs that must survive worker restarts.

topic_groups.title: Software Supply-Chain Controls
topic_groups.selection_rationale: September 10 GitHub releases add programmatic AI security rollout, cache least privilege, and an immediate model deprecation; this is a concrete change-control lane after yesterday’s broader governed-operations coverage.

sources.title: AI Scan for pull request APIs
sources.why_selected: Security posture can be rolled out selectively and repeatably instead of through manual UI changes.
sources.usefulness: Create a staged security-control rollout for generated patches across Buildn and client repositories.

sources.title: Control GitHub Actions cache access with cache-mode
sources.why_selected: Cache poisoning becomes a permission design problem with explicit defaults and warnings.
sources.usefulness: Add cache-mode to agent-generated workflow templates and review it as part of CI hardening.

sources.title: MAI-Code-1-Flash deprecated
sources.why_selected: A model name in an agent workflow is a dependency with a retirement date, not a harmless string.
sources.usefulness: Maintain a model inventory with owners, alternatives, evaluation status, and migration dates.

sources.title: AI Scan security detections documentation
sources.why_selected: Controls are only useful when teams know what is detected, where, and with which review path.
sources.usefulness: Turn detection coverage into a client-facing acceptance matrix rather than a generic “AI security” claim.

topic_groups.title: AI Misuse + Evaluation Boundaries
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Anthropic’s September 10 threat report and its August incident follow-up add fresh evidence that autonomy, persistent memory, and evaluation misconfiguration must be governed together.

sources.title: Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026
sources.why_selected: It argues AI changes the economics and tempo of familiar abuse, with multi-agent workflows and persistent state increasing scale.
sources.usefulness: Use the report as input to a client tabletop covering identity theft, tool abuse, memory poisoning, and rapid re-deployment.

sources.title: Improving our alignment and security efforts
sources.why_selected: It shows that sandbox assumptions, monitoring, prompt boundaries, and partner controls must fail independently, not as one brittle layer.
sources.usefulness: Build a preflight checklist for every Hermes or client evaluation that can reach a network, filesystem, or credential.

sources.title: PentAGI reference in the threat report
sources.why_selected: Public orchestration lowers the expertise and labor required to compose reconnaissance and exploitation tasks.
sources.usefulness: Use it only as a defensive fixture for tool-boundary and detection testing in an isolated environment.

sources.title: METR independent review reference
sources.why_selected: External review is a useful pattern when the system owner also designed the evaluation environment.
sources.usefulness: For client pilots, separate builder, operator, and reviewer roles even when the pilot is small.

topic_groups.title: Research Agents + Formal Evidence
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A material update to recent accepted-work coverage: OpenAI’s September 8 Navier–Stokes report adds a formal Lean repository and a public correction/update trail, shifting the question from agent output to inspectable proof artifacts.

sources.title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
sources.why_selected: The output is paired with formal verification and a public qualification boundary, making review more concrete than prose alone.
sources.usefulness: Use the pattern for evidence packs: raw output, executable check, human judgment, and a correction log.

sources.title: Lean formalized proof and repository
sources.why_selected: Executable checking creates a stronger handoff than a static narrative, even when the result remains under review.
sources.usefulness: For client analyses, attach runnable validators, source snapshots, and environment versions where feasible.

sources.title: Research acceleration: the view inside OpenAI
sources.why_selected: It frames agent leverage around accepted experiments and decisions, not token count alone.
sources.usefulness: Track accepted artifacts, reviewer time, retry cost, and correction rate in Buildn work.

sources.title: OpenAI Navier–Stokes paper PDF
sources.why_selected: A dossier should distinguish the announcement from the underlying evidence and preserve both links.
sources.usefulness: Use source-level linking to keep summaries auditable and easy to revisit.
